showcase.title: Image Splitter for structured batch slicing
showcase.subtitle: Split one or many images using guides, patterns, color detection, and smart export presets.
tips: Preview is based on the active image, but export applies your split rules to the entire queue.
Preset changes auto-sync in workspace mode with a short debounce, so your latest setup is preserved.
Advanced methods like color match and auto sprite analyze image pixels and can be heavier on RAM and CPU.
Use ZIP export for large runs, or one-by-one download when you need direct per-file browser saving.

faqs.question: Does preview only affect the selected image?
faqs.answer: Preview renders on the active image so you can validate the split plan quickly. When exporting, the same split configuration is executed across all queued images.

faqs.question: How do Basic mode methods work (count, percent, pixel)?
faqs.answer: Basic mode uses uniform cuts: count splits into N parts, percent uses fixed percentage steps, and pixel uses fixed pixel intervals.

faqs.question: When should I use pixel/percent pattern methods?
faqs.answer: Pattern methods are ideal for repeating non-uniform slices, such as alternating card layouts, where each step can follow a custom sequence.

faqs.question: What is Color Match best used for?
faqs.answer: Color Match scans lines for target color ratios and is useful for finding natural separators like white gutters. For best performance, tune tolerance and safe-zone values.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Custom List and Social Carousel?
faqs.answer: Custom List cuts by explicit guides from edges, while Social Carousel builds ratio-based slices for social posting and supports crop, stretch, or pad overflow handling.

faqs.question: When should I use Auto Sprite mode?
faqs.answer: Use Auto Sprite for transparent sprite sheets. It detects alpha islands, then extracts and sorts bounded regions based on connectivity and sort mode.

faqs.question: When should I choose ZIP versus one-by-one export?
faqs.answer: ZIP is best for large outputs and cleaner download flow. One-by-one is useful when you need immediate individual files, and the app will confirm before very large download counts.

tooltips.colorMatchGridFallback: Color Match only works with a single axis. Grid is currently treated as horizontal splitting.
tooltips.colorMatchOffset: Moves the cut position away from the detected matching line/column. Positive values cut later, negative values cut earlier.
tooltips.colorMatchTolerance: How close a pixel color must be to your rule color to count as a match. Higher values are more lenient.
tooltips.colorMatchSkipBefore: Requires this many consecutive matching lines/columns before the current one before a cut is allowed.
tooltips.colorMatchBreakAfter: After a cut is created, skip this many lines/columns before checking for the next cut.
tooltips.safeZoneVarianceThreshold: Lower values are stricter and avoid busy lines. Higher values accept more detail.
tooltips.safeZoneSearchRadius: How far to slide up/down (or left/right) from the detected line to find a safer cut.
tooltips.safeZoneSearchStep: Distance between candidate lines while searching for a safe zone.
tooltips.spriteAlphaThreshold: Pixels with alpha strictly greater than this value are treated as solid sprite pixels.
tooltips.spriteMinArea: Ignore tiny islands smaller than this area to reduce noise.
tooltips.spritePadding: Expand each detected sprite bounding box by this padding.
tooltips.orderDialogLiveSequence: This text reflects current horizontal/vertical direction and priority axis.

tooltips.remainderHandling:
• Crop: Crops the remainder to fit the exact ratio.
• Stretch: Stretches the final slice to cover the overflow.
• Pad: Pads the final slice with a solid background color.
